kjv: his master shall bring him unto the judges
mine: his master shall bring him to God
note: ha'elohim is "God" (perhaps at the sanctuary, or household gods at the doorpost). The KJV follows the Targum in reading it as "judges". Same issue in 22:7-8.
naqom yinnaqem means "he (the slave) shall be avenged", implying blood vengeance or the death penalty. "Punished" leaves the penalty vague.

kjv: so that her fruit depart from her, and yet no mischief follow
mine: so that her children come out, but there is no serious harm
note: weyatse'u yeladeiha ("her children come out") may mean premature live birth or miscarriage, and the 'ason ("serious harm") of vv. 22-23 may refer to the mother, the child, or both. The passage is much debated, and both renderings keep it ambiguous.
